name: trend-machine
base: data/v1/ relative to the site root. Works on any static host; no auth, no keys, no rate limits.

trends.description: All topics, full editorial dossiers: angles, hooks, sources[], first_seen/last_seen, stale + seeded flags. The canonical record — sort by opportunity_score desc for the hottest plays.
trends.notes: Seeded topics (seeded:true) carry researched starting-point figures in their summaries — treat as baselines, not live measurements.

trends_flat.description: Flat consumer feed: opportunity-ranked, stale topics excluded. Lightweight 'what to make content about today' list. Every item carries 'velocity_trend': snapshots/delta/since plus a ready-made inline SVG sparkline (wave 8) — honest 'building' state when fewer than 3 snapshots exist.

trends_flat_sample.description: Clearly-labeled SAMPLE (sample:true) derived from seeded topics — for consumer development only, never the live path.

trends_flat_js.description: JSONP twin of the flat feed — trendsCallback({...}). The CORS-safe fallback for pure static hosts that cannot send Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers.

velocity.description: Hourly velocity/opportunity snapshots per topic, ascending by timestamp. Classify with assets/js/trajectory.js (UMD — loadable in node).
velocity.notes: Snapshots are real pipeline observations; topics with <3 snapshots are still building history.

platform_velocity.description: Wave 6: per-platform hourly velocity series per topic ({topic_id: {platform: [[iso, vel], ...]}}). Starting points — series build one snapshot per refresh; trajectories classify after 3+ per-platform snapshots.
platform_velocity.notes: Empty/missing series mean 'still building history', never a guess.

meme_formats.description: Wave 9: the tracked meme format families — hand-curated from Oct-2026 web research (verified = 2+ independent sources; single-source = one source or creator lore, flagged). Each family carries current examples with evidence URLs and the live topic ids whose text matches the family this run (tracked_topics — derived, never stale).
meme_formats.notes: Topics link back via their format_family field (null when unmatched).

seed_freshness.description: Wave 14: the seed-freshness sweep — every seeded topic checked for staleness: source URL liveness (HTTP probe; dead = GET 404/410 only — HEAD rejections fall through to GET, timeouts never mark stale), store corroboration (last_seen <= 7d), and velocity tracking (a seed with <3 snapshots but a first snapshot <6h old is warming up, not stale). Verdicts: healthy / stale-source / stale-untracked / flaky-warning.
seed_freshness.notes: Generated by scripts/seed_freshness.py (not in refresh.sh — run as a periodic audit).

lifecycle.description: Ignition/burnout lifecycle layer: every topic's current lifecycle stage (building/steady/warming/igniting/peaking/cooling/burned-out) classified from its real velocity snapshots, per-topic stage ribbons, and the last-24h ignitions/burnouts boards. Stages use the classifier's own thresholds (ignition line v=70, rise/fall ±1.5/hr) — readouts, not predictions.
lifecycle.notes: Stages are computed from the same velocity snapshots as data/v1/velocity.json; the boards show transitions that actually happened in the last 24h.

board.description: Wave 39 (VP-0011): the One-Look Creator Board — the homepage's first screen as data: the ranked make-now picks (creator-makeable, stale excluded) with evidence chips and the angle to make, straight news labelled and listed apart, the phenomenon merges the build applied, and the opportunity index's honest definition (an index 0-100 — velocity discounted by saturation — never a percentage or a view promise).
board.notes: Derived from the canonical store every build; the store itself (data/v1/trends.json) keeps all tracked topics, merged listings included.

live_wire.description: Wave 28: the Live Wire — a command view over the pipeline's own stored outputs: every refresh lane with its real recorded hit count and health (live / degraded / stale-skip / skip-by-design, exactly as the pipeline records it), plus the hour's top movers computed from stored velocity snapshots only.
live_wire.notes: Written by scripts/build_live_wire.js (runs in refresh.sh after build_site.py); human-readable on live-wire.html.

streamer_desk.description: Wave 29: the Streamer Desk — sourced streamer directory, dated updates, a drama tracker that prints only multi-source-verified timelines (unverified claims quarantined with reasons), streamer houses with dated rosters, and an events calendar whose past/upcoming status is computed from dates.
streamer_desk.notes: Written by scripts/build_streamer_desk.js (runs after build_live_wire.js in refresh.sh); human-readable on streamer-desk.html.

changelog: 0.8.0 (2026-10-13): Prediction layer RETIRED by direct order — the Oracle pages, the scorecard page, the forecast-explorer board page, the forecast endpoints, their data payloads and their schemas are removed from the served site and the build; the site now tracks ongoing hype only (the creator board, the Live Wire, the Streamer Desk, lifecycle stage readouts). The forecast ledger file stays in the repo as an archived record, unlinked. 0.7.0 (2026-10-13): Wave 39 — the One-Look Creator Board. New data/v1/board.json endpoint: the homepage's first screen as data — ranked make-now picks with evidence chips and angles, straight news labelled apart, phenomenon merges (additive view only; the canonical store keeps every tracked topic). Additive only, no shape changes to existing endpoints. 0.7.0 (2026-10-12): Wave 17 — Oracle layer 2. New data/v1/lifecycle.json endpoint: every topic's ignition/burnout lifecycle stage (building/steady/warming/igniting/peaking/cooling/burned-out) classified from its real velocity snapshots with the classifier's own thresholds (ignition line v=70, rise/fall ±1.5/hr) — readouts, not predictions; per-topic stage ribbons; last-24h ignitions/burnouts boards. Additive only, no shape changes. 0.6.0 (2026-10-11/12): Wave 13 — the two missing wave-9 seeds land: turn-to-your-neighbor and zayn-sleeping-photo, verified live against Know Your Meme (both entries updated within the day) and meme.com's meme library. Wave 14 — ledger health: forecast resolution gains a terminal 'unverifiable' verdict (48h passed, <2 actual snapshots — counted separately, never in the hit rate) with full evidence recorded (window bounds, point counts, thresholds); the resolution rules live in one shared module (scripts/resolution-lib.js) used by both the hourly pipeline and the standalone scripts/check_resolutions.js audit. New data/v1/seed-freshness.json endpoint: the seed-freshness audit (scripts/seed_freshness.py) verdicts every seed healthy / stale-source / stale-untracked / flaky-warning with per-source probe results. Additive only. 0.5.0 (2026-10-11): Wave 9 — Oracle accuracy scorecard becomes a full page (the scorecard page): honest pre-resolution states, per-horizon accuracy table, by-call breakdown, recent resolutions, current 48h projections, and the resolution method — all rendered live from the forecast accuracy payload, with the hit rate shown only after 10+ forecasts resolve. New meme-format family tracking: data/meme_formats.json curates 12 hand-researched Oct-2026 format families (verified/single-source flags kept honest), pipeline/format_families.py matches topics to families by conservative keyword rules (re-computed every run), every topic carries format_family, dossiers show a family chip linking to formats.html, and data/v1/meme-formats.json publishes the families with their live topic links. Additive only, no shape changes. 0.4.0 (2026-10-11): Wave 8 — velocity sparkline history UI + 'Remix this' exporter polish. Every flat-feed item now carries 'velocity_trend': snapshot count, first/latest velocity, delta, tracked-since label, a pre-rendered inline SVG sparkline, and per-platform mini-summaries — all from real snapshot data; topics with <3 snapshots report state 'building' with no fake line. Dossier pages gained per-platform mini-sparklines and a <details> snapshot data-table for screen readers; the dashboard table gained a sparkline column. The remix exporter is now a pure unit-tested function (pinned fixtures) and copies best platforms too. Additive only, no shape changes. 0.3.0 (2026-10-11): Wave 7 — Oct-2026 trend-drop refresh: 12 new topics (SocialPilot Sept 25–Oct 10 re-check: Did I Win This Trend?, 31 Days of Halloween, Halloween Home Tour, Creepy Fact Storytime, DIP ON EM, #CityTasteTest, Homecoming Proposal Reveal, girl in red 'we fell in love in october', Memo Boy 'Insomniac', Spooky Scary Skeletons remix, Patient Zero TikTok Search Hub, pumpkin patch season); new 'trend_type' field on every topic (format/topic/format+topic, rule-derived from format_tags + category); seeded topics carry a 'verification' flag (verified/single-source/unverified — unverified topics render name-only sources with a confirm-live note). Bow Bow Bow re-graded to Peak/saturation-high. Additive only, no shape changes. 0.2.1 (2026-10-11): Oracle 2.0 — forecasts.json records now carry confidence basis (snapshot count + fit quality), signal attribution (velocity delta, slope, accel, recency, cross-platform spread, fired thresholds), and per-platform trajectories (additive only, no shape changes). New data/v1/platform-velocity.json and the forecast accuracy payload (the Oracle's own forecast-vs-actual log; 'building history' until 10+ forecasts resolve). 0.2.0 (2026-10-11): index.json endpoints are now objects {path, description, schema, updated, records, notes} (was plain path strings). Added flat-feed, JSONP, velocity entries; draft-07 schemas for every endpoint under data/v1/schema/.
usage: GET data/v1/trends.json, sort by opportunity_score desc for the hottest plays. Start at data/v1/index.json for the full endpoint map.
